text:
jordan-cs: Customer (ACME) escalated — streaming responses intermittently reorder after client reconnect. They see partial chunks, then older tokens stitched in, and sometimes duplicate pieces. Happening on both Python and TS SDKs. Request ID: req_0a1b2c3d. Reported ~2:15pm PST.
jordan-cs: Example from their app logs: 
```
// timeline extracted from app
[14:14:12] open stream -> got: 'The model predicts that'
[14:14:13] disconnect (network blip)
[14:14:13] reconnect -> resume -> got: ' with high confidence.'
[14:14:13] later: 'predicts that the user will'
```
jordan-cs: They said billing shows two partial responses billed separately. Customer worried about duplicate charges + bad UI UX.
maya: Thanks — pinging eng-streaming, @sam for SDK regression triage :eyes:
maya: Did they upgrade SDK recently or change network proxies?
sam: Noticed a small batch of releases last week for iterator resume in both py/ts. Could be related. Which SDK versions?
jordan-cs: Py 0.12.1, TS 1.3.0. They tried downgrade to py 0.11.9 and said Python looked better but TS still exhibits ordering.
alex: Can you ask for a minimal repro? Ideally an eventstream capture (SSE frames) and client logs showing last_event_id and any Resume-From headers. If they can share a small transcript that'd help.
jordan-cs: Sent SSE capture and app logs to the ticket — uploaded to the support portal. Link: https://support.redwood/acme/INC-7123 (internal).
ivy: Quick guesses: 1) client-side buffer re-emit on reconnect, 2) server-side duplicate tail when KV cache isn't synced to resumed session, 3) streaming resume handler may replay prefix tokens from a previous partial response.
sam: I'll look at iterator resume code path. On TS we changed the reconnect backoff and introduced a small in-memory chunk queue. Might be re-emitting chunks on race.
sam: Can someone paste the raw SSE events from the capture here? Need to see event IDs and ordering.
jordan-cs: Pasted snippet from capture: 
```
event: message
data: {"id":"evt-101","delta":"The model predicts"}

// disconnect

event: message
data: {"id":"evt-102","delta":" with high confidence."}

event: message
data: {"id":"evt-100","delta":" predicts that the user"}
```
jordan-cs: Note evt-100 ended up after 102 in the app.
maya: That looks like out-of-order delivery on resume. Could be server-side if resume cursor points to an earlier segment. @support-bot can you surface the infra logs for req_0a1b2c3d ?
support-bot: Fetching logs for req_0a1b2c3d... (this may take a minute)
support-bot: Logs pulled — trace shows: 
```
[worker-7] stream_open session=ses-9abc seq_start=100
[worker-7] emit evt-100
[worker-3] resume detected for session ses-9abc, resume_from=101
[worker-3] replay from 101 -> emit evt-101, evt-102
```
sam: Interesting — two different workers emitted overlapping ranges: worker-7 emitted evt-100 earlier, worker-3 resumed from 101 and replayed 101..102. That explains duplication and ordering. Looks like resume_from cursor calculation was off by one under low-latency race.
alex: That matches a regression I fear: the resume cursor logic was tightened for KV eviction last week. If resume_from is using last acknowledged event id (and the client acknowledges last_event_id before disconnect), race between ACK processing and in-flight emits could lead to stepping back one event.
ivy: If server replays 101..102 and client still receives 100 after reconnect, final ordering becomes 101,102,100 -> as seen.
sam: Repro plan: I'll craft a unit test that simulates a disconnect during emit with two workers and assert resume_from uses highest persisted offset. Also test edge where client ACK is processed concurrently.
alex: In the short term, mitigation options for CS: 1) recommend client dedupe by event id on-receive (idempotency), 2) advise to pin to py 0.11.9 which avoids the TS queue repro, 3) if customer needs immediate fix, we can enable single-worker affinity for their session (manual) to avoid cross-worker resume races.
jordan-cs: ACME wants single-worker affinity for now and a patch timeline. Can we do that?
maya: Yes — ops can toggle affinity for req namespace. @sam estimate for a fix?
sam: If root cause is resume cursor off-by-one, patch should be small — 1–2 days including tests + canary. I'll open PR and include backport to 2024.12 branch.
ivy: Also add a short-term server-side dedupe at emit layer to drop repeats when replay overlaps recent emit window. Low-risk guard.
alex: I'll coordinate lab canary on staging and run their SSE capture repro against it.
maya: Great. Jordan — I'll update the customer: offer single-worker affinity and suggest dedupe client-side as a temporary measure. ETA for patch ~48 hours.
jordan-cs: Customer confirmed accepts affinity and will do client dedupe. Thanks team.
sam: Action items: sam -> PR and tests; alex -> staging canary + run ACME capture; ivy -> add emit-layer dedupe guard; maya -> update ticket and ops run affinity toggle.
sam: Adding note — also check billing path: duplicates may have led to >1 billable partial token blocks. Need billing-team FYI to reconcile if necessary.
maya: Ping @finance later.
ivy: I'll draft a brief postmortem after patch and include reproduction steps + logs.
maya: Thanks all :tada:
